rationale: Restored one explicit knowledge use that the last rewrite dropped while keeping every other field as it stood. The account's closing sentence relies on the vote path taking its claim from the node's in-memory last log, which is recorded in the entry on election log sources, and that entry was no longer listed as used by the current interpretation even though the source ids and the reasoning were unchanged; nothing else about the account was edited.

interpretations.rationale: The question asks whether the follower keeps an in-memory last log index its store no longer holds and whether ordinary AppendEntries can bring it back; both halves are answered, and the answer to the second is now sharper than refusal alone. After the conflicting append with the store failure armed (receipt 3448bd1c64244c3b884b24c7bad8a8bf, injected case, conflict index 1) the node's last log index was 3 while its store held only index 1 and no longer held index 2, and it answered Success false with that stale index. Ordinary AppendEntries then go two ways. The whole-log append from index 1 - the shape the leader's builder produces once its rejections have walked nextIndex back to one - was refused (index 2, Success false, store still at index 1), because the conflict loop trusts the stale in-memory index, looks the missing entry up in the store, misses and returns. But the shape a leader sends while its nextIndex is still one past that stale index, a single entry 4 behind previous index 3, was accepted with Success true (index 3): the store now holds index 4 above a gap at 2 and 3, the node's last log index is 4, and the leader reading that response advances that peer's nextIndex, records its match index and never sends the range again. The control accepted both shapes and kept a contiguous store from 1 to 4 (indices 5 to 7), so the injected failure is what produced the gap. The mechanism is the same source path in all three phases: the abort returns before setLastLog, the in-memory last log stays ahead of the store, the conflict loop treats any index above it as new without reading the store, and the abort also refreshes no contact. What remains source-read rather than measured is a live leader walking its nextIndex down and the effect of the stale index on the node's own vote claims, which the vote path takes from the same in-memory fields.
counterevidence: The trigger is a store error on one RPC, and the library's leader path treats the same error as a reason to step down and to fail the caller, so a store error may be intended as a condition that takes a node out of service rather than one a follower must survive in place.

The requests in the receipt are supplied by the probe; the leader's own builder produces those shapes at the corresponding nextIndex values, but no live leader walked its nextIndex down in this receipt and the interval that takes is unmeasured.

The snapshot path still repairs the peer once the leader's log no longer holds its nextIndex, and a restart removes the stale index while the store's own last index is still below the deleted suffix; the restart is not a repair once an entry has been stored above the gap, because the in-memory last log is initialised from that same last index and the hole stays hidden.

In this three-entry probe the gap covers only user entries; nothing here shows what the leader does with the acknowledgement beyond its own bookkeeping, and the control shows the same requests are handled normally when the store does not fail.
limitations: Two executions of the same lineage, eight events in the latest, two cases and three request shapes each; the outcomes were uniform but the probe does not vary the failure point, the number of retries, or the timeouts, which were two seconds for heartbeat, election and lease.

The account depends on a supplied fault - a store whose StoreLogs returns an injected error for the append that follows a truncation in the same RPC - and says nothing about torn writes, a lost acknowledged write, or a monotonic store.

The contract is disputed in the counterevidence above: the same store error leads the leader path to step down, so an operator may be expected to restart the node instead of relying on in-place repair.
That a hole above which an entry is stored survives a restart is read from the initialisation path rather than measured, and the probe never restarted a node.

The consequence of the gapped store beyond this node - what a leader does with a match index for it, or what happens if it campaigns or is asked for the missing entries - is inferred from the source and not measured.

knowledge.assertion: The aborts that can follow a suffix deletion in the same RPC return without advancing the in-memory last log, so the follower keeps an index its store has lost.
A successful response advances the peer's nextIndex past the accepted entry and records its match index where voters are counted.
A node judges and claims elections with its in-memory last log, never with a fresh read of the log store.
